rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was tested after the angels and explained the presented things to them in detail by naming them.
rows.anchor: Âdem onları isimleriyle ber-tafsil anlattı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reply to Adam's naming spells out His prior claim to know the unseen and what the angels disclose or conceal.
rows.anchor: Ben size, ‘her hâlde ben bütün semâvât u arzın gaybını bilirim’ demedim mi?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed reply explains the earlier summary that God knows what the angels do not; a genuine summary and its detail have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: evvelki إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ kavl-i celîlinin mânasını tafsil ve tefsir etti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angelic speech is truly a matter of meaning, not verbal or nominal forms; otherwise a statement made in summary would not amount to its detailed version.
rows.anchor: melâikeye olan kelâmın hakikati ancak mânadan ibarettir, suver-i lafziye ve ismiye değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immediate purpose is specifically to establish and manifest the wisdom and causes of Adam's fitness for vicegerency, which the angels had not grasped.
rows.anchor: bilhassa [317] Âdem aleyhisselâm’da tahakkuk eden devâ‘î-i hilâfeti takrir ve izhâr-ı hikmet ü kudrettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God connects His acts to hidden causes and wisdom, yet no creature can claim entitlement through a cause: He creates causes and grants outcomes, and His will is the true original cause.
rows.anchor: Sebeb-i aslî ve hakīkī ancak O’nun iradesidir. Hikmet de O’nun lâzımıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God announced Adam's vicegerency to the angels summarily, as if consulting them, then trained Adam through teaching the names.
rows.anchor: melâikesine istişare eder gibi icmâlen tebliğ etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested Adam and the angels together, exposed the angels' inability, proved Adam's fitness in practice, and prepared them to submit to him.
rows.anchor: geçirip melaikeye izhâr-ı acz ve ona bilfiil isbât-ı ehliyet ettirmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story clearly and subtly reveals how divine lordship manifests, recalls inward blessings embedded in human nature, and leads into the later direct-address warning.
rows.anchor: rubûbiyyet-i ilâhiyenin tarz-ı tecellîsi büyük bir vuzuh ve pek ince bir üslup ile ifham edilerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel is Jacob's epithet; the author records several readings of the name and reports Hebrew meanings including God's chosen one or servant of God.
rows.anchor: “İsrâil” Hazret-i Ya‘kūb’un lakabıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Israel is said in Hebrew to mean God's chosen one or servant of God.
rows.anchor: İbranî’de bunun mânası safvetullah veya abdullah demek olduğu beyan olunuyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the Jews as descendants of a chosen servant of God is meant to spur the people of Torah to believe.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın güzide bir kuluna evlâdlıkla muzâf olan ehl-i Tevrât!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's blessing includes recollection in the heart and on the tongue; the Israelites sought blessings yet had forgotten even the blessing itself.
rows.anchor: asl-ı ni‘meti bile unutmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost blessing is guidance through scripture and prophethood, culminating in awareness of Muhammad's mission and the divine guidance brought by the Hijra to Medina.
rows.anchor: bunlardan başlıcası فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًۭى mazmûnunca kitap ve nübüvvete işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant made since Adam's descent and confirmed through the Torah required following, believing, and obeying the source of guidance God would send, especially the final Prophet Moses foretold.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın haber verdiği Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ’ya iman edecektiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Muhammad fulfills God's covenant, and God in turn fulfills theirs by admitting them among those without fear or grief.
rows.anchor: Resûlüm Muhammed’e ittibâ‘ile îfa ediniz ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an confirms the Torah in the essentials of faith, and the Israelites should believe in it and bring all their deeds into accord with it; it recalls Adam's story.
rows.anchor: esâs-ı îmân itibariyle yanınızdaki Tevrat’ı musaddık olarak inzal eylediğim Kur’ân’a iman ediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelites should have been the first to recognize and affirm revelation and prophethood, rather than becoming the first disbelievers.
rows.anchor: Ni‘met-i vahyi, ni‘met-i nübüvveti ilk anlayıp tasdik edecek olan siz olmanız lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must not exchange God's signs and miracles for a few coins or petty worldly interests; faith brings blessings far greater than what they fear losing.
rows.anchor: Benim âyetlerimi, mucizelerimi semen-i kalîle satmayınız, birkaç para gibi hasis dünya menfaatlerine değişmeyiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God alone in verse 40 addresses common people and elites, while verse 41's command to take refuge in God is directed particularly to elites.
rows.anchor: onun avam ve havâssa umûmî ve bunun havâssa husûsî bir hitâbı istihdaf etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mixing truth with falsehood and knowingly concealing truth is a broad prohibition covering both intellectual and practical conduct, though its immediate address targets scholarship.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetin mefhûmu pek şümullüdür. İlmî ve amelî husûsâta şâmildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition extends from scholarly fraud and distortion to deceptive commercial dealings and unjust judicial rulings.
rows.anchor: Bilgiçlerin tedlislerine, tezvirlerine ve tahriflerine, hatta ehl-i ticâretin karışık mu‘âmelâtından ve hâkimlerin haksız hükümlerine varıncaya kadar hepsine şümûlü vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelite scholars mixed their own writings, interpretations, and translations with the original Torah and hid earlier-scripture verses describing Muhammad.
rows.anchor: evsâf-ı Muhammediye hakında yaptıkları gibi kütüb-i sâlifedeki âyetleri saklıyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They replaced the Torah with their own translations and followed desires instead of pursuing truth in learned matters, spreading confusion and deception.
rows.anchor: kendi yazdıkları tercemeleri “işte kitâbullah” diye Tevrat yerine koyuyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse alone suffices to set Islam's scholarly course: keep the Qur'an distinct from translation and treat tafsir and interpretation as such; translations never become the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ı Kur’an, tercemesini terceme, tefsir ve tevili de tefsir ve tevil olarak bellemek ve belletmek bir farîza-i hak bulunduğu unutulmamalı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites are told to establish prayer and give zakat.
rows.anchor: salâtı ikāme ediniz ve zekâtı veriniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bowing with those who bow means joining the Muslim congregation in prayer; it signals both that this is Islamic prayer and that congregational worship is required.
rows.anchor: cemâ‘at-i müslimîn ile beraber rükû ediniz, eğiliniz, rükûlu namaz kılınız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bowing prayer is distinctive of Islam, and the prayer units are named rak‘as in relation to bowing; here bowing conveys the sense of praying.
rows.anchor: rükû ile namaz dîn-i İslâm’a mahsustur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews and Christians go directly from standing to prostration in their prayers and do not bow.
rows.anchor: Yehûd ve Nasârâ namazlarında kıyamdan doğrudan doğruya secdeye giderler, rükû etmezler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexically, bowing means inclining the neck together with the back; in religious law it means bending at the waist to a right angle while maintaining composure.
rows.anchor: şer‘an itidâli, belinden bir zâviye-i kāime vaziyetinde bükülmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bowing completes the movement from standing to prostration and makes Muslim prayer a spiritual ascent with bodily reverence and composure.
rows.anchor: Kıyamdan secdeye kapanmakta bir itidâlsizlik vardır ki bunu rükû itmam eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orders and prohibitions addressed to Israel apply beyond them: Islamic law contains them, and Muslims too must believe and obey them.
rows.anchor: hükmü onlara mahsus değildir. Şerî‘at-i İslâmiyede bunlar vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe Medina Jewish scholars who privately affirmed Muhammad as true and urged others to follow him, but feared losing gifts and taxes; some urged charity, obedience, prayer, and zakat without practicing those duties themselves. The author says one or all such cases occasioned the verse.
rows.anchor: asr-ı sa‘âdette Medine’deki ahbâr-ı Yehûd’dan bazıları kendilerine gizlice gelip “Muhammed hakkında ne dersin?” diye istifsar edenlere “doğrudur, haktır” derler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse asks how people can command abundant goodness while forgetting themselves even as they continually read the Torah; the author also renders the question as asking whether they will learn sense.
rows.anchor: Acayip, siz nâsa birr yani bol bol iyilik emreder de kendinizi unutur musunuz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reason is practical contradiction: the purpose of enjoining good is to guide others, but neglecting oneself deprives oneself of guidance and risks damnation.
rows.anchor: başkasını irşad edip de kendisini unutmak ve kendisini iyilikten, irşaddan mahrum etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second reason is that a teacher who will not heed his own advice refutes himself and his learning, while misleading people he claims to guide; this is another contradiction and a kind of deception.
rows.anchor: kendisi kendi emrini, kendi nasihatini dinlememek, kendini ve ilmini fiilen tekzibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third reason is that acting against one's advice destroys its value and alienates listeners, like cutting the branch one sits on.
rows.anchor: verdiği emr ü nasihatin kendisi hilâfını yapmak onun kıymetini kırmak ve herkesi ondan tenfir eylemektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining good remains good and obligatory; the verse censures forgetting oneself, but does not forbid a sinner from sincerely advising others when he speaks truthfully. It sharply warns preachers to take themselves seriously first.
rows.anchor: bu âyet fâsığın doğru söylemek, sözünde cidden iyiyi söylemek şartıyla vaaz etmesini, emr bi’l-ma‘rûf yapmasını men‘etmemekle beraber

rows.speaker: Buhârî ve Müslim
rows.claim: They report a man brought on Judgment Day and cast into the Fire, where he circles like a millstone; when asked why he preached good and forbade evil without practicing it, he admits his hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: Buhârî ve Müslim’de bu babda şu hadîs-i şerîf rivayet olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birr means broad goodness: as a noun it is abundant good and as a verbal noun expansion in goodness, derived from a word for spaciousness; it encompasses every good.
rows.anchor: geniş iyilik, bol bol iyilik etmek demek olan “birr” her türlü iyiliğe, her nevi hayra şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies birr into three kinds: worship of God, care for relatives, and good dealings with friends.
rows.anchor: birr üçtür: Allah’a ibadette birr, akrabaya riayette birr, ahbâbına muâmelede birr.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This exhortation ratifies Islam's high moral and intellectual seriousness, especially for scholars, rulers, and judges; its placement after prayer, zakat, and congregation points to their effect on moral refinement and criticizes scholars who do not practice their learning.
rows.anchor: bilhassa ilmiyle âmil olmamak Benî İsrâil ahbârının şi‘ârı olduğunu anlatmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When these commands feel difficult, people should seek God's help through patience and prayer.
rows.anchor: ihtiyâcâtınıza sabr u salât ile isti‘âne ediniz.
